subject: Workplace Skills
title: Framing as Strategic Alignment
description: A 60-second lesson on Framing as Strategic Alignment.

hook.text: An engineer wanted to refactor old code. Her boss said no. She reframed it as reducing outage risk by 40%. Approved.

buildup.text: Leaders think in terms of strategic priorities: risk, revenue, customer impact, and competitive advantage.

discovery.text: Reframing your proposal in their strategic language is not manipulation. It is translation from your world to theirs.

twist.text: The proposal didn't change. Only the framing did. The same work was rejected as maintenance and approved as risk.

climax.text: Before pitching anything, ask: which strategic priority does this serve? Lead with that connection explicitly.

punchline.text: Speak their strategy. Your idea will land.

quiz.question: Why was the code refactor approved only after reframing?
options: The engineer offered to do it for free
The reframe connected it to a strategic priority the boss cared about
A different boss approved it the second time
